summary: bible/characters/index.json lists gender 'unspecified' for three characters; gender must be male or female (it anchors voice casting and image generation). The appearance cards set a value; the index should match.

findings.basis: Source text: ch007-p66 'The Dormouse slowly opened his eyes. “I wasn’t asleep,” he said'; ch011-p71 'Suppress him! Pinch him! Off with his whiskers!'
Source text: ch002-p23 'trembling down to the end of his tail'; ch012-p69 'the frightened Mouse splashed his way through the neighbouring pool'
The source only ever says 'it'. Inferred from H1 ruling 5.3 B: the Cat is the dream echo of Dinah, whom Alice calls 'she' (ch002-p22).

impact: voiceprint/voice casting and 06-art/character-concept read gender from both files; a mismatch lets one of them fall back to a default.
requested_action: character-manager updates the three index.json gender values through memory-bible (WRITE_RULES.md §5 controlled change). Not edited here: index.json is outside 03-characters/appearance's write scope.
ruling: Accepted. Dormouse = male (source 'his', ch007-p66; not inferred). Mouse = male (source 'his tail', ch002-p23; not inferred). Cheshire Cat = female (inferred: the source only says 'it'; derived from H1 5.3 B, where the Cat echoes Dinah, whom Alice calls 'she', ch002-p22). This follows directly from a signed ruling, so no new creative ruling is needed.
fix_instruction: In bible/characters/index.json (your file, Phase 3, not locked): set gender 'male' on CHAR-dormouse and CHAR-mouse, cite ch007-p66 and ch002-p23, and remove 'gender' from inferred_fields if present. Set gender 'female' on CHAR-cheshire-cat, add 'gender' to inferred_fields, and set reason to 'Source uses "it"; female follows H1 5.3 B doubling with Dinah ("she", ch002-p22).' Keep values identical to the appearance cards. Then close this ticket in your result.json.
